question.text: A hot air balloon is carrying some passengers, and a few sandbags of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> each so that its total mass is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>480</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math>. Its effective volume giving the balloon its buoyancy is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>V</mi></math>. The balloon is floating at an equilibrium height of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. When <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>N</mi></math> number of sandbags are thrown out, the balloon rises to a new equilibrium height close to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>150</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> with its volume <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>V</mi></math> remain unchanged. If the variation of the density of air with height <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>h</mi></math> from the ground is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>ρ</mi><mfenced><mi>h</mi></mfenced><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mfrac><mi>h</mi><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mfrac></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo></math> where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ρ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>25</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>6000</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo>,</mo></math> the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>N</mi></math> is _________.
